featured_reviews.name: Vasanth Pragash
featured_reviews.review_text:
November 2025 review

Pool is big and possibly olympic size. The pool has various depths starting from shallow end of 4 feet to over 15 feet depth. The pool is trifurcated into three areas, 1) Shallow end ,2) 2 Full length lanes( this reduces the width of the pool for the other 2) 3) Main pool area. Small lockers, shower rooms etc are available at no extra cost.

Membership process:
Full the details online in the website, be sure to upload aadhaar and pay the amount. For verification you will need aadhaar copy, printout of 2 receipts(one will become your id), original copy of doctors medical certificate stating you have no skin diseases or communicable diseases and are fit to swim, and three passport photos.They will take aadhaar copy, both receipt copies,the doctors medical certificate and photos. You will recive an SMS that registration is done and they will give you back one stamped receipt with your photo as your medical id. Laminate it or keep it in a ziplock bag.

Advantages:
1) Very friendly staff. They are extremely courteous and helpful in resolving pool queries and so on.
2) Very convenient timings. 6AM-12 noon (11-12 ladies only) and 5-10PM (5-6PM ladies only)
3) Pool is maintained very clean despite its public nature.

Disadvantages:
1) Nothing is provided, no soap, towels or paper.
2) You will need to bring your own locks, lockers are very small so make sure you buy a small lock.
3) Restrictions apply on swimwear , no full body suits for anyone and men can only wear swim shorts. No cotton shorts, etc allowed. If you come in morning you can buy swimming shorts, goggles and swim caps from the reception but it could be expensive.
4) Pool is extremely clorinated, and you can feel it in your teeth and hair. Be sure to brush and clean yourself as soon as your done with swimming. No shower doors for showers.
5) This is a public pool, which means a lot of people will be using it, this is understandable but can cause problems if your trying to swim laps as many kids/adults will crash your path. If this is the case stick to pool area 2).

Best time to swim would be 9-11 in the morning as a guy, most people are working and the sun is bright such that the pool isn't too cold.

featured_reviews.name: Ryan Rodricks
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently completely refurbished and opened back to the general public.

Pool - 50 Metre Olympic spec. size with starting boards and lane markings (underwater).
Max depth- 17 Feet
Minimum Depth - 4 Feet
Lanes - 10
Access ladders - 6

The pool itself is very very good. The water is clean, minimal chlorine and no skin infections or rashes like you sometimes get with dirty water. The water filters seem to be working effectively.
Rules
Only swimers allowed onto the swim area level and around the pool.
Swimming costume is compulsory.

The facilities are well maintained, the staff are helpful and the overall experience is very good.

Timings
Morning 06.00am to 11.00am
Ladies 11.00am to 12.00pm

Evening 06.00pm to 10.00pm
Ladies 05.00 to 06.00pm

Overall Swimming Experience - 3/5

The Swimming experience itself is quite a mess. Filled with senior citizens/ middle-aged aged men with absolutely no sense of how a swimming pool works.
This is comparable to Mumbai traffic but in water.
People swim in any direction, breadth wise, diagonal wise, criss-crossing from anywhere and just getting into each other's way. There is absolutely no concept of swimming in a 50M pool and the crowd is comparable to a Waterpark on weekends.

If you're a casual swimmer just looking to get wet on a hot summers day then it's perfect.

If you're a professional swimmer looking to put in some practice laps when not coaching, then you will be disappointed.

It's impossible to actually swim 50M uninterrupted. Whatever the batch time.

The BMC should allocate a set timing slot morning/evening for serious swimmers only. Easier said than done though as its a common pool and arguments are bound to arise.

Overall the facilities are very good and the experience is nice but for competition level swimmers looking for extra practice it's not worth the time.

One of Mumbai’s most well-planned and versatile sports complexes. It truly stands out as a one-stop gymkhana offering an impressive range of facilities under one roof.

The infrastructure is modern, clean and well maintained, creating a great environment for training and recreation.
A big highlight is the Sollasa Sports Café, which serves quality food at reasonable prices—perfect for a healthy meal or quick snack after a workout or a game.
The Sports Recovery Centre is another major attraction, featuring Sauna, Steam, Massage and Hydrotherapy facilities, giving athletes and fitness lovers a professional space to recover and rejuvenate.
The Terrace Turf is ideal for a quick game of football and cricket, offering a great playing experience with a city view.
Complex also has at least two well-sized halls that are perfect for engagements, birthday parties, naming ceremonies, society meetings, and small get-togethers.

The pool caters to various age groups and skill levels, offering batches throughout the day.

Beyond swimming, the complex has developed into a multi-sport hub. It features facilities like pickleball courts, carrom tables, a small cricket turf, and even a well-equipped gymnastics hall, attracting young athletes and hobby players alike. There is also a small sports shop inside the premises where basic sports equipment and accessories are available.

One of the highlights many visitors appreciate is the canteen. Known for its omelette and poha, it serves fresh, satisfying snacks and also offers a decent missal that regulars enjoy after their sessions.

The place is fairly well maintained and serves as a much-needed sports center for the residents of Vile Parle. With its growing range of facilities and community-friendly atmosphere, it continues to be an important recreational and fitness landmark in the locality.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Prabodhankar Thackeray Udyan in Vile Parle East is a small, green escape tucked beside the Prabodhankar Thackeray Swimming Pool. Built thoughtfully over what was once a dump yard, the transformation into a public garden has made it a popular spot for morning and evening walkers. The park sees a steady flow of senior citizens who enjoy the peaceful environment and leisurely strolls. Long benches line the pathways, allowing tired walkers a comfortable place to rest and enjoy the surroundings.

Inside the garden, there is a small Ganpati temple where people stop to pray, adding a spiritual touch to their daily routine. A modest playground area exists for kids, which is a great idea in concept, but unfortunately the maintenance leaves much to be desired. Several of the play structures are either broken or worn out, and the toilets, too, are not in the best condition.

On the positive side, the garden is rich in greenery and offers a refreshing environment. You’ll often come across many friendly cats that have made this space their home, adding a charming, albeit quirky, touch. Two-wheeler parking is convenient outside, while car parking can be quite challenging, especially in the mornings. Vendors selling fresh juices and soups outside the gate make it a pleasant stop after your walk.

featured_reviews.name: Thomas Lewis
featured_reviews.review_text:
If Google allowed 0 stars, that is exactly what this experience deserves.

I initially received a call from someone based in Lucknow who shared a brochure promising free room nights through hotel tie-ups and international trips to Bangkok, Pattaya, and other East Asian destinations. Based on these promises, I was asked to visit the Country Club office in Andheri/Kandivali.

At the office, I met a salesperson who confidently told me that I had come to the right place and repeated all the attractive promises shown in the brochure. Based on this sales pitch, I ended up paying ₹1.5 lakhs for the membership, along with an Annual Maintenance Charge (AMC) which has to be paid every year.

Once the payment was done and the membership activated, the reality turned out to be completely different.

First, I discovered that I had also been enrolled into a timeshare arrangement, something that was never clearly explained during the sales discussion. I had already paid ₹10,000 separately for an “international trip package”, which was supposed to cover my international travel benefits. Essentially, I had already paid for everything that was promised as part of the membership.

Second, the Country Club website shows a long list of hotels and partner properties, creating the impression that members have access to a large network of stays. The truth is that **most of these properties are either not available when you try to book or come with additional charges.

Third, the company claims a wide network of resorts, but in reality they only have around 8–10 of their own properties. The rest are so-called “associated properties” where members still have to pay ₹2,000–₹3,000 per night or sometimes even more**.

So the obvious question is: if members still have to pay for rooms, then what exactly are we paying AMC for every year?**

There are no real “free rooms”, and most of the benefits highlighted during the sales presentation simply do not exist in practice.

This entire experience feels like a classic high-pressure sales trap filled with exaggerated promises and misleading information. Once the payment is done, the story changes completely.

My strong advice to anyone considering this membership: stay away and do thorough due diligence before paying even a single rupee. The promises made during the sales pitch do not match the reality at all.
